versions.summary: Links each provider's current terms and explains how the gateway's, the serving provider's and your own key's terms apply to the route you choose.
Discloses the Experiential Labs promotional route for Free-plan chats, what it captures and how its provider may use that content. Accounts were asked to accept the terms again.

Adds how the Google connectors access, use, store and share Google user data, and states compliance with the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. Product analytics now also covers usage events from the AGI apps recorded against your account, so a consent given under an earlier version covers page views only.
Adds the checks the referral program runs and their lawful basis, and states how many user-scoped tables account erasure covers.
Adds how Free-plan chats on the Experiential Labs promotional route are captured and how its provider may use them.
Appeals can be filed in the product or through the appeal form, each with a reference, as well as by email.
Describes the website's Skip approvals default and the actions that still need your review.
Corrects where the identity provider's cookies come from and removes a browser storage entry the product no longer writes. Visitors were asked to choose again.
Fly.io now also runs our malware scanner, which every uploaded file passes through and which keeps no copy.
Corrects the Experiential Labs entry against its current privacy and data-controls documents and records the Free-plan promotional route.

Adds the signed-in refund request, the 14-day withdrawal in the EU, EEA and UK, a once-per-account refund within 7 days when no credits were used, and the hold during a payment dispute, and corrects how plan upgrades are billed.
Adds the in-product Report an accessibility barrier ticket beside the email address.
Adds product usage events, sent only in managed-cloud mode and only after you allow product analytics, as a data category, and removes the statement that no usage event leaves your device.
Adds the Impersonation section and an impersonation option on the report form.
Attached files, project knowledge files and selected connector context now count as untrusted content, so a turn that holds them asks before anything could send data out.
Updates the website's default authority to match the account policy, keeping fail-closed checks and workspace boundaries.
